children: UBS named its top consumer discretionary stock picks even as the firm remained relatively cautious on spending due to subdued real wage growth, lower immigration, limited pricing power, tariffs, and low savings. "High operating leverage, accelerating GLP-1 adoption, and elevated price sensitivity add to the pressure, particularly for retailers and legacy department stores," warned UBS, although hotels were seen as a bright spot amid support from upper-income consumers.

is UBS' top pick across beverage, household, and personal care product names. "We believe KO has the ability to deliver +MSD organic revenue growth and +LDD underlying EPS growth, which compares to peers delivering +LSD revenue and EPS growth, standing out in a group where core growth is becoming scarce. While the stock trades at a low-30s premium vs. peers (vs. 5-yr historical premium of +LSD), we believe this premium relative to history is warranted given the degree of earnings visibility and upside," updated UBS.
In the fitness sector, Life Time Group

was the top pick, with UBS' price target of $57 implying ~37% upside. The near-term debate on LTH was noted to be on average member per center growth, and whether they can continue growing average center revenue per center membership and ultimately the impact on comparable center revenue.
Looking at food names, J.M. Smucker Co.

was tagged as the top pick. "In our view, SJM operates in categories that have demonstrated favorable growth characteristics relative to center-store packaged food over time. Specifically, we think that the company's top-line outlook could ultimately prove conservative as (1) management is still forecasting coffee volumes down LSD despite incoming deflation, and (2) segment momentum is improving across the board, with other portfolio brands delivering sequential improvement as we move through the year," highlighted the UBS analyst team.
cruised in as the top pick. Viking

was called a pure play in luxury travel with a strong balance sheet. The view on VIK is that it has scarcity value for investors that look to invest in the luxury consumer, but specifically a consumer of luxury experiences rather than luxury goods.

We expect the combination of robust comp sales, higher merchandise margins, and fixed cost leverage will drive a ~26% 5-yr. EPS CAGR," highlighted UBS.

title: Coca-Cola, Viking, and Aritzia are top consumer picks at UBS amid economic headwinds
